capabilities.title: Durable run/step journal + tool-call loop (waiting_for_tool)
capabilities.notes: Этап 2.7 (ТЗ §8.3): the kernel journals every generation step in generation_steps (migration 6: ALTER TABLE generation_runs ADD COLUMN pending_tool_call_json + generation_steps table, no rebuild) and streams generation.step events (provider_turn/tool_call/tool_result/final_commit). A provider turn emitting a tool call is validated against the declarative tool registry (capability + minimal JSON-Schema argument check) and durably transitions the run to waiting_for_tool — a DERIVED wire status from the pending marker (DB status stays streaming; the v3 CHECK is untouched). The kernel NEVER executes tools: the host performs the effect and submits generation.tool.result, which journals the tool_result step, clears the marker and resumes the provider turn with the assistant tool_calls + tool-role messages. Stable terminal codes: TOOL_NOT_FOUND / TOOL_ARGS_INVALID / TOOL_LOOP_LIMIT (8 calls max) / TOOL_RESULT_STALE (non-idempotent submission). M5 slice 4 adds CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE pre-negotiation (ТЗ §9.3): a run whose provider does not declare tool support fails with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before any network request instead of silently degrading to a no-tools turn; new wire error code, kernel_capability_negotiation.rs (3 integration tests: honest providers.list declarations, fail-before-generate probe, tools-capable pass-through). Crash-at-wait: fresh lease survives a reopen and the result still resumes; expired lease → interrupted (retry-safe). Этап 2.8: waiting-run cancel/retry — generation.cancel finalizes cancelled itself for a waiting run (no live executor) and every terminal writer clears the pending marker; retry from a cancelled waiting run starts attempt 2; retry on a still-waiting run is GENERATION_RUN_STATE_CONFLICT. Tools register via Kernel::register_tool; generation.tools.list (app.read) serves the registry. Tests: 7 tools.rs unit + 2 fake unit + 2 adapter + 10 tool_loop.rs kernel integration + 1 providers_openai tool round trip + 1 storage migration test. Этап 2.9: desktop host Integrated — the packaged kernel smoke registers a tool and completes a full waiting_for_tool → tool.result round trip over the real Tauri host path (NEOTA_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1); the host seam KernelHost::register_tool was added, and both Tauri-local and remote-http stream pollers now close the consumer stream when a run durably waits (previously an unbounded poll loop). Honest boundary: JSON-Schema validation covers a documented subset (object/required/additionalProperties + scalar/array/object types); the full schema engine is a follow-up. Этап 2.10: the facade exposes `generation.tools.list` / `generation.tool.result` on every NeoBackend implementation (LocalBackend over the wire; the closed backend rejects with UnsupportedError — there is no legacy route; RemoteBackend over the SDK); M5 slice 41 (ТЗ §13.2): the web chat now distinguishes tool execution from text streaming — streamWireGeneration forwards the durable generation.step announcements to onStep, ChatPage derives the active tool from tool_call steps (input.toolCall.name only; arguments/results never reach the UI) and renders a ToolActivityBadge while the run is waiting, clearing it on the next provider_turn/tool_result step and on done/error/stop; generate.test proves the step forwarding, ToolActivityBadge component tests (2), i18n en/ru. М5 slice 43 (ТЗ §8.3, §13.2): the Settings panel gains a Tools tab rendering the declarative tool registry (generation.tools.list) — name, description and required argument names from each input JSON-Schema, with an honest empty state (no tools registered by this host) and never rendering arguments/results; useGenerationTools hook (queryKey generation-tools), ToolsPanel component + 2 tests, i18n en/ru (settings:tools, tools:*). M5 slice 47 closes step rendering in the transcript: the durable run-step UI (RunTranscriptPanel over generation.events) renders tool_call and tool_result steps with sequence badges, status and attempt markers (chat:runStepType_tool_call/runStepType_tool_result, i18n en/ru). Remaining tool UX: result submission from the UI (generation.tool.result — the desktop kernel smoke round trip stays host-side) and the consent modal for dangerous tools remain Этап 4. M5 slice 57 (ТЗ §8.3/§9.3): the desktop host now performs safe built-in tool effects — setup_local_kernel_mode wires the declarative app_now contract (UTC clock; side-effect-free, consent-free — no ТЗ §14.2.3 high-risk category) and the BuiltinToolExecutor seam; the stream poller offers every durably waiting tool_call step to the executor and, when handled, submits generation.tool.result itself and keeps polling the durable journal through the resumed turn (the kernel stream already sent its terminal notice at the wait point). Failures stay recoverable: an executor error or a failed submission leaves the run durably waiting (the kernel stale-result guard makes double submission harmless); unhandled tools behave exactly as before (stream closes, run waits). SEC-07: only the tool NAME reaches diagnostics — never arguments or result content. Tests: executor.rs unit (app_now answered, unknown tools stay waiting, step extraction only on waiting tool_call steps, RFC3339 conversion) + host_tool_executor.rs integration (full tool round trip completed by the host executor with resumed final text; no-executor control keeps waiting_for_tool). capabilities.title: Content-addressed asset store (put/get/content/delete, avatar linkage)
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 5 remainder (ТЗ §5.1 AssetStore port, AGENTS.md §11/§12): canonical assets over Product Wire (73 ops total). assets.put publishes immutable bytes under a content-derived managed key <kind>/<sha256>[.<ext>] via the crash-safe neotavern_storage::assets publisher (temp-write + sync + atomic rename + registry INSERT, symlink-safe resolution, orphan GC) and is an idempotent re-import — identical bytes under the same kind return the existing record with deduplicated:true (AGENTS.md: import must not create duplicates). assets.get returns metadata, assets.content returns the ORIGINAL bytes base64 (never lossy; the 4 MiB wire response limit caps the servable size, larger assets are addressed by relativeKey through host transports), assets.delete removes the registry row first (orphan GC covers the file). assets.thumb (image audit stage C, 2026-09-06) generates a kernel-side aspect-preserving thumbnail (JPEG q82 / PNG by alpha, maxPx 16..1024, decode preflight 64 MiB / 16384 px / 64 MP) with the AGENTS.md §12 disk cache under <data-root>/cache/thumbnails keyed sha256-maxPx-version (atomic temp+rename, deletable, rebuildable) — the UI hydration path no longer transfers multi-MiB originals through assets.content. Avatar linkage is now writable: characters.create/update accept avatarAssetId and the kernel verifies the asset exists (stable ASSET_NOT_FOUND). Thumbnail CACHE generation (AGENTS.md §12 rules 4-9) remains the web/legacy side — the canonical plane deliberately has no image codec dependency; the thumbnail key contract (<original hash>+<size>+<algorithm version>, never regenerating when the key is unchanged) is documented and tracked within slice 5 remainder. 5 kernel tests cover round-trip, dedupe, avatar linkage, delete->not-found and validation. M5 slice 7 remainder web: the NeoBackend facade gained the AssetsApi (get/content/put/del) — the last wire domain without a facade surface, so every Product Wire operation is now reachable through the typed facade (ТЗ §13.1). LocalBackend forwards over the kernel transport with request/response validation, RemoteBackend forwards over the ClientSdk, closed backend throws UnsupportedError (the legacy plane has no assets route — avatars/backgrounds remain legacy-raw until their own cutover). Parity + validation tests (68 neobackend). M5 slice 6 (ADR-0046 waiver 8 assets part): the legacy converter now maps avatar ORIGINALS into the canonical store — characters.avatar URLs (`/api/v2/assets/avatars/<sha256>.<ext>` or the thumbnail variant) resolve to `<data-dir>/files/avatars/<sha256>.<ext>`, the file is published as a `avatar` asset via the crash-safe publisher inside the conversion transaction (neotavern_storage::assets::publish_asset_in_tx) and `characters.avatar_asset_id` is linked; a missing file or unrecognizable avatar string is reported as an orphan (never silently dropped), and pre-avatar legacy schemas contribute 0. The legacy avatar string itself is still not copied verbatim (ТЗ §34 avatar→asset). Storage tests: avatar conversion round-trip + missing-original orphan in the legacy suite. API key resolved at execution time from the config's secret_ref through the SecretResolver seam (Kernel::set_secret_resolver) and passed via ProviderRequest::api_key — only in the Authorization header, never in body/DB/logs; missing resolver fails closed. Registration via the new Kernel::register_provider seam; config instance selection in the run model. Этап 2.7: serializes declared tools (function schema) and the resumed-turn tool context (assistant tool_calls + tool-role result), accumulates SSE tool_calls deltas into normalized ProviderEvent::ToolCall. Этап 2.8: kernel integration test drives the full tool round trip over the real SSE path — turn 1 streams a normalized tool call, the kernel validates and durably waits, generation.tool.result resumes turn 2 with the tool context, the run completes with exactly one assistant message; both HTTP bodies are asserted (tools serialization + resumed tool_call_id). M5 slice 4: the adapter declares its honest capabilities (tools/streaming true; vision/thinking/jsonMode false — no silent downgrade) via the new ProviderAdapter::capabilities port method; wire.provider.capabilities surfaces it in providers.list. М5 slice 48 (auto-hydration + UI selection): the kernel now materializes adapters from STORED configs — every providers.config.set registers (or replaces, by adapter id, no duplicates) the matching adapter right after its commit, and startup hydration re-registers all saved configs, so a configured openai instance is generatable immediately and survives restarts without host-side wiring (kernel tests: config survives restart + full generation run on the restarted kernel, re-save replaces). The web wire transport resolves the selected provider config id (settings active-provider-config-id) into the provider/model pair handed to generation.start (generate.test 9); a vanished config is an honest PROVIDER_CONFIG_NOT_FOUND, never a silent fake fallback. Honest boundary: executing a configured key still requires the host SecretStore/SecretResolver seams — desktop host wiring remains a follow-up slice; without a seam, setting a key fails closed (SECRET_UNAVAILABLE) and a run resolves fail closed (ProviderError::Unavailable). The Anthropic adapter remains the documented TS-side SDK exception (packages/provider-sdk), legacy contour — the canonical plane has no Rust Anthropic adapter yet, and capability declaration makes that absence honest at the list surface.

capabilities.title: Plugin network broker (SSRF policy + bounded streaming)
capabilities.notes: SEC-03/SEC-04 (M1 Wave 1 + Wave 2 + Wave 3): plugin network.http.fetch and socket destinations pass the §29.1 SSRF scope policy — every DNS answer checked, bracketed IPv6 and IPv4-mapped literals normalized, per-hop redirect re-checks, connect to the policy-approved IP with the hostname only in Host/SNI and post-connect remoteAddress verification; response bodies are capped while streaming and the connection is destroyed on exceed (apps/plugin-runtime/src/host). Wave 2 (SEC-04): global and per-plugin in-flight byte budgets (NETWORK_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES_GLOBAL=64 MiB, NETWORK_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES_PER_PLUGIN=16 MiB, worst-case reservation per fetch body NETWORK_MAX_BODY_BYTES) fail a NEW request with the stable NETWORK_INFLIGHT_LIMIT before its body is read, and release on success/error/cancel; two host tests cover both budgets (including a cross-plugin global trip with 8 concurrent held fetches). Wave 3 (SEC-03): the verified-IP set is now honored on EVERY connect — direct fetch, HTTP absolute-form proxy hops (verified IP in the request-target, Host keeps the hostname), HTTPS CONNECT tunnels (verified IP in the CONNECT authority, TLS validates the hostname), tcpConnect, udpSend AND WebSocket (the undici WebSocket was replaced by a socketHandles RFC 6455 client that connects to a policy-approved address, verifies remoteAddress after connect and performs the HTTP Upgrade itself — no DNS for the hostname in the stack). M5 slice 45: the legacy (Rev4) network.fetch RPC (apps/server/src/plugin/backendHost.ts fetchRpc) previously resolved DNS inside fetch with only a hostname allowlist — a plugin holding network:* could reach loopback / cloud metadata through a hostname or an IPv4-mapped literal. It now runs the same resolved-IP policy via safePluginFetch (apps/server/src/lib/safePluginFetch.ts): ALL DNS answers classified, bracketed IPv6 and IPv4-mapped hex/dotted literals normalized (::ffff:7f00:1 == 127.0.0.1 denied), connection to the pre-verified IP with the hostname only in Host/SNI, post-connect remoteAddress re-check, redirects re-policed (<=5), bodies bounded in bytes (10 MiB, SEC-04) and a 30s deadline; private ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7, CGNAT) stay allowed exactly like the plugin-installer download policy. Tests: safePluginFetch.spec.ts 18 (classification incl. hex-mapped, all-answers fail-closed, verified-IP connect, post-connect race destroy, redirect re-policy, oversized body, plus fetchRpc integration: loopback/link-local/mapped/metadata denied even with network:*, localhost denied via DNS, allowlist/scheme/method validation).

capabilities.title: Plugin package trust (signature/digest verification)
capabilities.notes: SEC-05 (M1 Wave 1): publisher Ed25519 signature + per-file sha256 digest verification before consent/install (format neotavern.package-signature.v1, apps/server/src/lib/packageTrust.ts); trust states built-in / verified-publisher / locally-trusted / unsigned-untrusted recorded in the plugin registry (migration 0023) and surfaced as InstalledPlugin.trust; NEOTA_PLUGIN_PUBLISHER_KEYS keyring + NEOTA_PLUGIN_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE policy; unsigned packages enabled via consent become locally-trusted; ZIP/tar.gz reject duplicate normalized paths, symlinks, traversal, encrypted entries and bounded zip bombs. Kernel-side trust registry roundup (M5 slice 52): the canonical registry also records the four SEC-05 trust states — plugins.rs/themes.rs trust_rank orders built-in(3) > verified-publisher(2) > locally-trusted(1) > unsigned-untrusted(0), an install that would LOWER the recorded rank is rejected with a stable TRUST_DOWNGRADE product code (plugins_install_never_downgrades_trust / themes_install_never_downgrades_trust), an unknown trust state violates the closed wire enum -> ContractViolation (x-wire-unknown-behavior reject), and the wire PluginDto.trustState / ThemeDto.trustState surface through translatePlugin/translateTheme as InstalledPlugin.trust / InstalledTheme.trust in the PluginsPanel and themes UI. built-in is a first-class state for future bundled extensions; the kernel currently ships no bundled plugins, so no row carries it yet — the state exists and is rank-protected, and the host-side package verifier that would feed verified-publisher/locally-trusted installs into the web transport remains the documented boundary (slice 50). M5 slice 60 (ТЗ §SEC-05): NEW crates/adapters/package-verify (neotavern-package-verify) — the host-side verifier the kernel install op already assumes (plugins.rs: host verifies signature + per-file digest + ZIP traversal/symlink/bomb rejection BEFORE plugins.install). PackageVerifier.verify(bytes): ZIP safety (path normalization rejects traversal/absolute paths incl. Windows drive/UNC, symlink entries via S_IFLNK mode, duplicate normalized paths, bounded entry count, declared-size and compression-ratio caps before any read, capped entry reads — zip bomb containment), manifest.json (bounded read, JSON) declaring id/version/permissions/files{path,sha256}, per-file SHA-256 digest equality with no-unlisted-payload enforcement, Ed25519 publisher signature (ring) over exact manifest bytes via manifest.json.sig with fingerprint-keyed known-publisher / locally-trusted key sets. Trust classification matches plugins.rs rank order (built-in 3 > verified-publisher 2 > locally-trusted 1 > unsigned-untrusted 0); a declared signature that fails to verify against any held key FAILS CLOSED (SignatureInvalid — never an implicit downgrade); an unsigned manifest is unsigned-untrusted and structurally verifiable. Permissions are NOT validated here (the granted set is the install consent moment, ARC-08). Verifier never extracts the archive. Tests: 14 unit incl. valid signed package (verified-publisher), locally-trusted, unsigned, bad signature, unknown-key signature fail-closed, traversal, absolute path, duplicate path, symlink-mode boundary (zip writer cannot emit S_IFLNK — real symlink archives covered by release fixtures), unlisted file, missing file, digest mismatch, zip bomb, trust-rank order; clippy clean. Packaged (round 42): the packaged golden smoke proves the SEC-05 fence behaviourally on the portable artifact — a probe plugin installed as verified-publisher is re-installed at a higher version with a LOWER trust state (locally-trusted) and the kernel rejects it with PLUGIN_TRUST_DOWNGRADE without mutating the registry (the row still reads 1.0.0 / verified-publisher), and an equal-rank version bump to 2.0.0 lands durably; the probe plugin is uninstalled at the end so the walk leaves no residue. DESKTOP DOWNGRADE — evidence audit (this cell was Packaged, now Implemented): no packaged artifact verifies a package signature. `crates/adapters/package-verify` (PackageVerifier.verify) has NO call site outside its own crate — no Cargo dependency from apps/, any other crate, packages/ or tools/ — so the premise of the kernel install op (that the host already verified the package) is never discharged on the packaged artifact. `run_golden_smoke` step 15b (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:2411-2488`) only exercises the kernel trust-RANK fence on plugins.install (a client-supplied trustState: a lower rank is refused with PLUGIN_TRUST_DOWNGRADE and leaves the row untouched, an equal-rank bump lands), which is a different mechanism from signature/digest verification. The legacy sidecar verifier (apps/server/src/lib/packageTrust.ts) exists but no packaged smoke or release script drives it either. MISSING EVIDENCE: a packaged step that installs a signed and an unsigned archive through the verifier and asserts accept/reject plus the per-file digest check. The Rust verifier unit suite (14 cases: signed/unsigned/bad-signature/unknown-key/traversal/absolute/duplicate/symlink/unlisted/missing/digest/zip-bomb/trust-rank) remains component-level evidence only. REMOVED round 76: the crate was deleted after the install path became a manifest descriptor — a package signature would verify bytes no plane reads; the trust-rank fence in `plugins.install` is what the product actually enforces.

capabilities.title: Restore maintenance lock (global maintenance mode)

capabilities.title: SecretStore (secrets out of the main DB, portable secrets.enc)
capabilities.notes: SEC-01 (M1 Wave 1): new SecretStore port package (packages/secret-store) with three explicit backends — portable encrypted secrets.enc (AES-256-GCM, versioned scrypt KDF, authenticated header, atomic writes, fresh nonce per write, machine-independent key derivation, lock/re-encrypt), session-only memory (no plaintext fallback) and a read-only env provider for headless (NEOTA_SECRET_*). Provider and plugin secrets no longer live in app.db: migration 0024 adds value_ref columns and the DB stores only opaque references (portable:/session:/env:), resolved at runtime via ctx.secrets (apps/server/src/lib/secretStore.ts, migration 0024). Pre-migration plaintext rows are imported at bootstrap (idempotent). A reference whose backend cannot produce the value surfaces SECRET_UNAVAILABLE_ON_THIS_DEVICE (422) — never a plaintext fallback; backups and profile exports contain no secrets. Kernel-plane port delivered (crates/secret-store, ADR-0040): canonical portable v2 format with Argon2id (m=64 MiB/t=3/p=1) + AES-256-GCM, authenticated header, staged re-encryption, cross-machine portability tests (15 tests). М5 slice 49 (desktop host seam): the Desktop kernel host now wires the kernel's SecretStore/SecretResolver port handles — a session-only MemorySecretStore + resolver (crates/adapters/tauri-local secrets module) — so providers.config.set apiKey commits for the session and generation resolves the key at execution time (SEC-01 explicit session-only interim: values live in process memory only, a restart clears them and the runtime reports the stable unavailable state until the key is re-entered; portable:/env: references and missing records fail closed with typed Unavailable, never plaintext; host tests 3 — session round trip, fail-closed kinds, kernel store writability). OS-vault / Android Keystore adapters and the full portable UX (passphrase prompt, auto-lock UI) remain M3 — when the vault lands, only wire_session_secrets changes. STATUS 2026-10-31 (honest): the OS-vault adapter LANDED with M5 slice 58 (desktop installed-mode default, NEOTA_SECRET_BACKEND override) — the 'remain M3' sentence above is superseded. M7 follow-up slice (headless): the headless host wires BOTH kernel seams for every backend (the previous store-without-resolver asymmetry is fixed — saved keys resolve at generation time) and gains the portable backend `--secret-backend portable --secrets-enc --secret-passphrase-file` (first-launch create, wrong-passphrase fail-closed startup, passphrase never over the wire; integration-tested). Remaining pre-Stable engineering tails (ТЗ §SEC-01.1, non-gate): no host opens portable secrets.enc on DESKTOP yet (desktop portable/smoke stays session-only interim; passphrase create/open UX is host-side), the Android Keystore store exists Kotlin-side but is not bridged into the kernel port (Android runs fail-closed unavailable). The v1→v2 scrypt converter of ADR-0040 §3 is DELIVERED (2026-10-31, secret_store::migrate::convert_v1_file — fail-closed, v1 file untouched, v2 target never overwritten); its host wiring follows the migration-contour slices.

capabilities.title: Plugin management UI
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 6 part 1 (M5): canonical Extensions-context registry over Product Wire (78 ops total) — schema v12 STRICT plugins table + 5 ops. The kernel durably records what the host ALREADY verified (SEC-05: publisher Ed25519 signature + per-file digest + ZIP traversal/symlink/bomb rejection stays in the legacy host packageTrust.ts) and what the user consented to: version, trust state (built-in / verified-publisher / locally-trusted / unsigned-untrusted), publisher key fingerprint and the GRANTED permission set — the install/update request IS the consent moment (ARC-08). Fail-closed: an install that would LOWER the recorded trust rank is rejected (stable PLUGIN_TRUST_DOWNGRADE product code — an unsigned package can never silently replace a verified one), same id+version re-install is idempotent, enable/disable are idempotent flag transitions, uninstall of an unknown plugin is PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND. M7 cluster 21 part 2: plugins.secrets.list|set|delete|reveal move the plugin own secret store onto the canonical plane with the SAME approved model as provider keys (SEC-01) - schema v28 plugin_secrets rows carry only the opaque SecretStore reference (namespace plugin-secret:<pluginId>, deterministic entry id per (scope, owner, key) so re-setting a key cannot orphan a value), every DTO is value-free with masked derived from the REFERENCE and never from key material, and the plaintext crosses the wire through exactly ONE op behind the host exposure policy (default OFF) plus the plugin secrets.reveal grant, with secrets.manageOwn for list/set/delete. The address rules are the KV state rules (chat requires an explicit ownerId), uninstall revokes the stored values BEFORE the rows cascade, and a host without a wired store answers SECRET_UNAVAILABLE on writes while the reference rows stay listable/deletable. Honest boundary: the React plugin sandbox never had a secrets host handler (the legacy routes served the legacy server-side plugin host), so there is no UI consumer yet. M7 cluster 21 part 1: plugins.state.get|set|delete move the plugin KV store onto the canonical plane — schema v27 STRICT plugin_state, one row per (plugin, scope, owner) with a CAS revision (a stale expectedRevision is REVISION_CONFLICT carrying the stored revision, never a silent overwrite), the documented 64-key/64-KiB quota enforced on write only, the scope resolving its owner (installation/user are singleton rows reported as an empty ownerId because the wire has no nullable field, workspace is the literal workspace row, chat REQUIRES an explicit ownerId) and every op gated by the capability the install consent recorded (PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND / PLUGIN_PERMISSION_DENIED). The plugin sandbox handlers (storage.kv.*) now read/write through this wire op on the kernel plane with the same capability gates and the same REVISION_CONFLICT/CAPABILITY_DENIED/NOT_FOUND errors, while the legacy plane keeps its REST route. Honest boundary: blob storage stays on the legacy plane on both transports because the wire v1 has no binary body. The table holds NO code, NO secrets and NO runtime handles — execution and cleanup (SEC-06) live in the isolated host executor behind the versioned capability protocol (ТЗ §14.1); themes (Theme SDK registry) and the legacy ST v1 translation remain slice 6 parts 2-3. 4 kernel tests cover the round trip, idempotent re-install, trust-downgrade rejection and wire validation. Slice 6 part 4 (M5): the web transport now calls the wire plugins ops — readPlugins/activatePlugin/disablePlugin/deletePlugin map the durable record (trust state + granted permission set fixed at the install consent moment) onto the legacy InstalledPlugin shape with honest neutral fields for what the wire row does not model (apiVersion 1 = does not advertise a higher SDK, has* surfaces false = not declared, compatibilityLevel native-v3); activation applies the RECORDED permissions and refuses a different requested set (CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE) instead of silently enabling with different rights; flows needing the host package verifier or the plugin executor (package install, git install, runtime safe mode, OAuth auth connections) are honest refusals — never a silent skip of SEC-05 verification or SEC-06 cleanup. safeMode is honestly false on the kernel plane (no kernel safe-mode mechanism). All 10 plugin hooks route through the transport. ui:api:check stays 64 sites (plugin routes were already parameterized through the client base). Статус поднят до Integrated (ARC-10, M5 slice 50): the Sidebar PluginsPanel and PluginSync manage the kernel plugin registry in kernel mode (list/enable/disable/uninstall through the wire ops, recorded trust state + consent-time permissions); package/git INSTALL, runtime safe mode and OAuth connections remain honest refusals (host SEC-05 verifier / SEC-06 executor not yet present in the web transport). M7 Etap-4 cluster 15: message-block attachments are durable on the kernel plane too — schema v25 `message_blocks` (one row per plugin→message binding with the immutable attach-time descriptor and the renderer state captured by blocks.freeze; both FKs CASCADE, so a message delete or a plugin uninstall leaves no orphans) served by chats.blocks.list (batched read, 100-id cap), chats.blocks.attach (explicit PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND instead of a raw FK failure), blocks.update (descriptor/state replace, clearSerializedState spells the legacy null patch, conflicting patches are VALIDATION) and blocks.delete. plugins/kernel/blocks.ts now persists through the wire bridge instead of legacyRaw, so the block host works on both planes; honest boundaries — descriptor/serializedState are free-form JSON OBJECTS on the wire (a scalar is refused, never coerced), and cross-client chat.message.block.changed push waits for the kernel event plane (cluster 18), so another client refreshes on its next load. Packaged (round 34): the DECLARATIVE plugin surface (data + blocks + state + secrets; ADR-0058 — plugins ship data, never markup/code in the kernel) walked in full on the packaged portable build: install with the consent-time grant list (storage.user / secrets.manageOwn / secrets.reveal), enable, chat block attach/list/update/delete, state set/get with optimistic expectedRevision + delete, secrets set/list (masked projection asserted plaintext-free) / delete, reveal proven to fail closed, disable + uninstall — exit 0. Plugins WITH executable code (the sandboxed code executor and jobs) stay OUT of this Packaged claim: the host-side executor adapter is program item 3 follow-up. Round 44 (cutover-registry row 21a): the plugin blob store joins the family — plugins.blobs.begin|append|finish|list|read|delete (schema v32 plugin_blob_uploads + plugin_blobs, ADDITIVE) replace the legacy /plugins/:id/blobs* HTTP store for the sandbox on the kernel plane. Bytes are chunked per ADR-0061 (declared length, sequential indices, 24 h TTL, staged outside the database), published content-addressed at plugin-blobs/<pluginId>/<sha256>.bin (identical bytes dedupe; the blob id IS the digest) and read back as bounded 256 KiB ranges so an 8 MiB blob never rides one JSON response. Ownership is enforced twice — the storage.blobs grant recorded at install AND the upload row's plugin — so a foreign upload id or digest is useless; the 8 MiB per-blob and 64-blob caps are kernel-enforced. The legacy route stays on the legacy plane until the stage-6 deletion. Packaged evidence (mechanism, not a date): `scripts/smoke-desktop-shell.mjs` boots the portable bundle (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/portable/*-portable/NeoTavern.exe`) with NEOTA_DESKTOP_SMOKE=1 NEOTA_KERNEL=1 and fails on any non-zero exit; `run_golden_smoke` step 15 (`lib.rs:2266-2410`) drives plugins.install, enable, disable, uninstall, plugins.state.get/set/delete, plugins.secrets.set/list/delete (with the reveal fail-closed assertion) and chats.blocks.attach/list + blocks.update/delete. capabilities.title: Plugin job queue (kernel-scheduled, execution gated)
capabilities.notes: ADR-0064. Desktop Packaged evidence: run_golden_smoke step 15b (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:2285-2341) enqueues one job for `smoke-plugin` with an opaque payload, lists it back by plugin (asserts exactly one), cancels it (asserts `cancelled`), and asserts the second cancel answers the product code JOB_TERMINAL; the walk runs inside the packaged portable artifact via scripts/smoke-desktop-shell.mjs (NeoTavern_0.1.0_x64-portable.zip, SHA-256 841ac496…4eca, exit 0). The runner itself is not started in the packaged default: no handler is registered, RunnerOptions::enabled is false, so jobs stay queued until the host adapter opts in — that is the documented kill switch, not a gap. Round 77 closes the packaged dispatch loop: `run_plugin_dispatch_smoke` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:250-372) runs inside the portable artifact when `NEOTA_PLUGIN_DISPATCH_SMOKE=1` — it installs a descriptor, enqueues one job over the wire, starts the real timer (`spawn_plugin_job_timer_inner`, 1 s tick, 30 s lease), waits for the emitted Tauri event, reports the outcome through `KernelHost::report_plugin_job`, asserts `plugins.jobs.get` reads `succeeded`, and asserts a drained queue hands out no second claim. Verified on the portable artifact SHA-256 57fd6274…8901 (printf shows `[smoke] plugin dispatch OK: enqueue -> claim -> due -> report -> succeeded`, exit 0); scripts/smoke-desktop-shell.mjs passes with the same env. Found and fixed there: Tauri rejects dots in event names (`IllegalEventName`), so the host channel is `plugin-job-due` while the app-event name the sandbox sees stays `plugin.job.due`. The webview half (sandbox `jobs.run` then `invoke('plugin_job_report')`) is covered by apps/web/src/plugins/kernel/jobs.test.ts.

capabilities.title: Themes
capabilities.notes: Этап 4 slice 6 part 2 (M5): canonical Theme-SDK registry over Product Wire (82 ops total) — schema v13 STRICT themes table + 4 ops. A theme is DATA, never code: opaque manifest + content-addressed CSS asset reference (cssAssetId published via assets.put kind theme-css, existence validated at install — the table holds no CSS bytes, no chats access, no keys, AGENTS.md §19). Single active flag names the applied theme; uninstalling the ACTIVE theme clears it so the shell falls back to the default (a broken theme must never block interface reset). Fail-closed mirrors plugins: version change that would LOWER the recorded SEC-05 trust rank is rejected (stable THEME_TRUST_DOWNGRADE product code), same id+version re-install idempotent, install never activates (activation is an explicit consent), unknown uninstall/activate is THEME_NOT_FOUND. Honest CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE remains where the wire contract cannot express the legacy flow: theme-package install (host-side SEC-05 verification must precede themes.install — no such host command exists in the web transport). Slice 6 part 5 (M5 slice 18): new wire op themes.deactivate (87 ops total) — the explicit 'stop applying a theme' consent (clears the single active flag, idempotent: no active theme is a successful no-op; the shell falls back to the default), distinct from uninstall which also removes the row. capabilities.notes: M6: `neotavern-headless` binds remote-http over a data-root Kernel. Loopback default, `--remote-exposure` + `--auth` for a public bind. Status is Integrated on the Web Client (remote-flow proven) and Implemented on the Headless host (CI binary, not a Released artifact). Android JNI local host can also connect here via URL/QR.
